We did fairly well in the senior match and Lowers won the 100 yards, while Basil Walden won the 220 1st string, with Des Mullen third in the 2nd string race at this distance.

The 100 yards saw Basil Walden and Gordon Lowers in front and Basil also won the 220 with Alan Picton in third place. Ches Walker won the 880 and Bob Taylor filled fourth place to score a point for us, but in the 440 yards Herne Hill had the first three home with Jim Heathfield first of our runners.

Basil Walden won the senior 100 yards and Frank Kemp followed suit in the junior event at this distance. Odde was second in the quarter and Gerry Trower won the junior 880 in good style and Ches Walker was also first home in the senior half-mile.
Basil Walden won the 220 yards with " Ginger " Holtum in third place and then Alan Picton won the 440, beating Ede of Epsom, the international runner.
Reg Bolam was third in the mile, with Bob Taylor fourth and Basil Walden was second to Pugh, of S.L.H., in the 220, with Des Mullen in third place.
Basil Walden sustained a damaged shoulder while playing “rugger” for Streatham recently, and we trust that the injury will not affect his track prospects this summer.
Badiali continue his good form to win this event very easily, and we were pleased to see Basil Walden making a welcome re-appearance on the track.

Thomas second and Alan Law third, while Alan Sexton regained the senior 220 title, with Frank Craft second and Basil Walden third. Derek Godfrey lost his junior 440 title to Peter Casselton, but it was a very good race and both these lads are champions of the future.

Basil Walden won the Southern Championship 100 yards and has showed himself our fastest sprinter for many years past. Alan Sexton has been experimenting with the quarter-mile in recent weeks, and will undoubtedly find that this is his true distance.

Bob Taylor won the 1 mile in 4 min. 28.5 secs., while Holtum and Basil Walden were first two home in the 100 yards. Ian Badiali won the 880 yards in fine style, beating Allen of Ealing H., the Middlesex champion, with Jack Brown and Ray Tooby also behind him.

Basil Walden ran 3rd in the Senior 100, while Denis Merrett was in a similar position in the 220 yards. Don Maclean ran his best race to date in finishing 2nd in the Senior 1 mile which was won in 4 min. 19.6 secs.
Basil Walden won the Club 75 yards handicap with John Smith 2nd and Eddie Lacey 3rd, while Stan Davies showed some of his old form when he won the 2 miles run off 280 yards in 9 min. 21 secs.

Basil Walden and Ginger Holtum both qualified for the final of the 100 yards, which Basil won with Holtum in 3rd place. Ray Tooby and Bob Taylor also qualified for the 880 yards final and Bob ran a fine race to finish in 2nd place, but Ray was almost run-out and could only struggle in for 6th position.

Stadium at Uxbridge, on 7th June, Basil Walden scored a fine win for the Club when taking the 100 yards title against strong opposition. His time was 10.2 secs and Basil's rugger training has certainly improved his sprinting powers, and he is running better now than at any time of his career.

Basil Walden won his 100 heat in 10.3 secs., and was placed 2nd to McDonald Bailey in the final which was won in 9.8 secs. Bill Lucas ran well to take 3rd place in the 3 miles run with Len Herbert in 6th place, but we had no finalists in the 440.
Basil Walden won both the Senior sprint events with Ian Badiali first home in the 880 in 2 min. 1.9 secs., and Alan Sexton winning the 440 in 52.1 secs.; shades of things to come!

In the 100 yards Basil Walden was our only runner and he caused some consternation by the fact that when he took his track suit off before getting on his mark, he discovered that he had forgotten to put his shorts on; was Basil's face red!

There was a 5-sided match on the programme, together with other events, also a local 100 yds. handicap, which Basil Walden won from the scratch mark in 10.4 secs.

Owing to Basil Walden and Denis Merrett being picked to run for the A.A.A. in Wales on this day, we were left short of sprinters and so could not field a team in the Senior 4 x 110 yds. relay championship.

Basil Walden was 2nd in the 100 yds., and Dicky Bartlett was 3rd in the 220. John Bromley won the 880 yds., and also finished 2nd in the 2 miles and so had a busy evening, and Bill Lucas was 4th in the latter event, with Len Bishop 2nd in the 880.
Basil Walden just beat Ron Holtum, with Pete Cornish in third place.
In the senior 4 x 110 yds., our team of Basil Walden, Ron Holtum, Denis Merrett and Ivan Mayers won their heat in 44.1 secs., the same time as the Polytechnic H., who were the eventual winners.

Our Club Championship Meeting, held at Battersea Park on Saturday, August 1st, was witnessed by a good crowd of spectators, who saw several new championship records set up. In the 100 yds., Basil Walden just beat Denis Merrett in 10.2 secs., which equalled the previous best time, with Ron Holtum in third place.

The sprinters did well with Basil Walden defeating the holder C. Gibbs, to win the 100 yards, with D Merrett 3rd and J.

Ron handed over to Basil Walden who put in a terrific challenge to hand over to Ivan Mayers about 1½ yards up. T.V.H. had Downs on the last leg and I thought he might rob us of our first win in this event but with 50 yards to go I saw Ivan's face break into a grin and I knew that it was ours.
Basil Walden won the 100 and 220 yards, Bob Walton won the 440 yards with Jock Cameron 2nd, I Badiali finished 3rd in the 880 yards and Ray Tooby was second in the three miles.
I think the biggest surprise was the defeat of Dennis Merrett by Basil Walden in the 100yards for Dennis has been showing good form this season.

"Take on all comers" Basil Walden, was the chief point scorer, for after winning the 100 yards in 10.7s and following Alan Sexton home in the 220 yards, he made a four point landing in the long jump to record 15ft. 8ins. for fourth place and followed this with an amble round in the 880 yards for 4th.

Belgrave's only win in the A.A.A. senior sprint relay championship came in 1954 when on July 31st at Birmingham the team of Dennis Merrett, Ron Holtum, Basil Walden and Ivan Mayers won their 4 x 110yds heat in 42.9 and then went on to take the final with the second best time recorded by a club team - 42.6.
